\section{Robustness to the Income Definition}
\label{sec:app-income-definition}

The baseline ranks households by total net household income. Table~\ref{tab:income-definition-robustness} tests whether this choice drives the measured inflation gap. We keep the household inflation rates, sample, consumption coverage, and weights fixed, and reassign national quintiles using equivalised income.

Equivalisation lowers the euro-area Q1--Q5 inflation gap from 1.4 to 1.1 percentage points in 2022,
but does not overturn the aggregate result that lower-income households faced higher inflation. The
larger changes in several countries show that household size can affect the composition of national
income quintiles and the magnitude of the estimated gap. This pattern is consistent with
\citet{klick2024equivalized}, who find for the United States that equivalisation substantially changes
the demographic composition of income groups but has only a minor effect on their annualised
inflation rates. In our setting, the robustness exercise therefore supports the qualitative baseline
result while clarifying that total-income quintiles measure household resources, whereas equivalised-
income quintiles provide a closer comparison of living standards.
